question: According to the unit, why is describing an effective teacher in terms of personality traits such as 'patience' considered less useful for trainees than describing observable behaviors?
options: Personality traits are difficult to measure accurately in a classroom setting
Patience cannot be practiced in the same way that a questioning technique can
Personality descriptions focus too much on the teacher rather than the students
Traits like enthusiasm are irrelevant to student learning outcomes
answer: Patience cannot be practiced in the same way that a questioning technique can

question: The unit explains that concept-checking questions serve a different function from comprehension-checking questions. What specifically do concept-checking questions verify?
options: Whether students have processed a procedural instruction before an activity begins
Whether students have understood the meaning of a word or phrase, not merely whether they can repeat it back
Whether students are ready to move from pair work to whole-class discussion
Whether students have memorized the correct spelling of new vocabulary items
answer: Whether students have understood the meaning of a word or phrase, not merely whether they can repeat it back

question: According to the unit, what is the specific risk when a teacher stops the whole class to correct one off-task student?
options: The corrected student is likely to become more disruptive afterward
The teacher loses the opportunity to use proximity as a management tool
The teacher has handed that student's inattention to every other student in the room
The lesson objective becomes unclear to the rest of the class
answer: The teacher has handed that student's inattention to every other student in the room

question: The unit argues that fairness in an inclusive classroom does not mean treating every student identically. According to the unit, what does fairness actually mean in this context?
answer: Fairness means giving each student the conditions in which she can participate on her own terms, rather than applying identical treatment to all students regardless of their individual needs.
